# Aṅgulimālattheragāthā (Thag 16.8)

**ID:** Thag 16.8
**Section:** Theragāthā (thag)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Aṅgulimālattheragāthā
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/thag16.8
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0508m.mul15.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Aṅgulimālattheragāthā* (Thag 16.8) is a poem in the sixteenth chapter (*nipāta*) of the *Theragāthā*, containing the verses of the elder Aṅgulimāla, the notorious bandit who was converted by the Buddha and attained awakening [SuttaCentral]. The text is translated into English by Bhikkhu Sujato and is preserved in ten translations across nine languages [SuttaCentral].

A large portion of the collection (§5.4–21.4) is shared directly with the canonical *Aṅgulimāla Sutta* (MN 86) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Several individual stanzas correspond to verses in the *Dhammapada* (including Dhp 26, 27, 80, 145, 172, 173, and 382), the *Kulattheragāthā* (Thag 1.19), and the *Saddhāsutta* (SN 1.36) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Both SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus identify broad cross-tradition parallels to these verses in the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G-Dhp), the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp), Sanskrit and Tibetan versions of the *Udānavarga* (including the Subaši manuscript and D 4099), and Chinese Dharmapada texts (T 210, T 212, and T 213), primarily in the *Apramāda-*, *Prakīrṇa-*, and *Udakavarga* sections [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].

Further parallels to the verses and the underlying narrative are found in the Āgama literature, including the *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99), the alternative *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 100), the *Ekottarikāgama* (T 125), and individual Chinese translations of the Aṅgulimāla story such as T 118 (*Fo shuo yangjuemo jing*) and T 119 (*Fo shuo yangjueji jing*) [DharmaNexus; Bingenheimer 2011]. In Pali commentary and grammatical tradition, verses are cited and commented upon in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Saddanīti* [DharmaNexus].
